title: Initialize Everything
prompt: Implement `int sum_known(const int *a, size_t n)` that totals the array — and if n is 0 returns 0. The trap: a wrong answer pattern is returning an uninitialized accumulator 'sometimes works'. Then implement `int *find_or_null(int *a, size_t n, int v)` returning the first match or NULL — the two functions together exercise init-discipline and null contracts.

tests.name: empty sums to zero
tests.hint: The accumulator must be initialized at declaration; the n==0 path proves it.

tests.name: sums and finds
tests.hint: Both contracts hold: totals and a NULL on miss.
